subject: Post-call: architecture constraints, noise tolerance, and gating criteria
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sana Ahmad <sana@medflowhealth.com>, John Walters <john.walters@medflowhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: architecture constraints, noise tolerance, and gating criteria

Hi Sana & John,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great overview of your telemetry volume and the regulatory constraints around PHI handling. Quick recap from our side and three asks to help us recommend the right hosting path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private):

- Recap:
  - Peak inference: ~1,800 qps internal, 30M tokens/day (90% ai-assisted summaries).
  - Regulatory: Must maintain customer PHI within a VPC boundary and have audit logs retained 2+ years.
  - Latency target: 95th <= 220ms for short-text summarization requests.

- Key constraints you flagged that affect tenancy decision:
  1) No cross-tenant PHI egress — cannot share GPU hosts processing PHI.
  2) Network segmentation — must terminate on your VPC and avoid public egress.
  3) Predictable tail latency for re-ranking flows (p95 SLO).

As next steps, can you do the following so we can validate options and produce a short technical recommendation:
  A) Confirm whether the 1,800 qps is burst or sustained (and the 1s/5s window shape).
  B) Share a redacted topology (or confirm if terminating in a partner cloud VPC is acceptable).
  C) Indicate whether your security team requires HSM/KMS integration (we can support either at Dedicated or Private tier).

I attached a one-page table that maps noise-tolerance and isolation controls (medflow-infra-constraints.pdf) and a sketch of how we’d place Dedicated vs Private in your network (network-topology-sketch.png).

If the asks above are heavy, we can run a short technical call with our infrastructure lead (Marissa) next week to go through the gating checklist. What times Tues/Wed look like for you?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: medflow-infra-constraints.pdf, network-topology-sketch.png
From: Sana Ahmad <sana@medflowhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: John Walters <john.walters@medflowhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: architecture constraints, noise tolerance, and gating criteria

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications inline and one doc attached.

- Burst vs sustained: the 1,800 qps is our burst peak from concurrent users; sustained is ~600 qps during business hours. Bursts last ~15–45s, several times per hour.
- Topology: we cannot accept any processing that allows PHI to leave our VPC in unencrypted form. Terminating in a partner cloud VPC is acceptable if we control routing (VPC peering or PrivateLink). See attached redacted topology (medflow_topology_redacted.pdf).
- KMS/HSM: required. We use an enterprise KMS (Azure Key Vault) and will need either KMS integration or a customer-managed HSM if using Private.

Additional ask: do you have historical p95 latency numbers for a 7B-class model on Dedicated under continuous bursting? That will help our SREs.

We can do Wed 11/25 10:00–11:00 PT for a technical sync with Marissa.

Sana Ahmad
VP Product
MedFlow Health

Attachments: medflow_topology_redacted.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: architecture constraints, noise tolerance, and gating criteria — prep for Wed 11/25 10am PT

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding Sana's reply and the redacted topology. Short internal prep notes below so we align on what to bring to the call: 

- Ticket: MEDFLOW-POC-02 (see HubSpot link).
- Important customer constraints to confirm on the call:
  * Burst characteristics (Sana confirmed bursts 15–45s; we should ask about concurrency patterns within the 45s window).
  * PHI boundary: they will only accept compute that completes inside their VPC or trusted peering link. Hosted API is likely out unless we can guarantee private termination; Dedicated with VPC peering or Private deployment are the primary fits.
  * KMS/HSM: they will require Azure Key Vault integration — map what we can support at Dedicated vs Private and what additional engineering is required.
  * p95 expectations: bring benchmarking data for our 7b-equivalent profile under continuous burst loads (we have historical numbers but validate on 7B quantized config).

- Prep deliverables for Wed:
  1) A short slide with Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs focused on network termination and KMS options.
  2) p95 latency table for 7B quantized on Dedicated under burst profile (we can use our redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx).
  3) Checklist for gating items to close before a Proof-of-Concept (POC): network peering, KMS access, SLO acceptance criteria, data retention/audit logs SLA.

I'll take the lead on the Dedicated vs Private slide; Marissa can own the SLO matrix and perf numbers. Lauren, can you confirm availability Wed 10:00 PT and take notes?

Karthik

Attachments referenced: redwood-slo-matrix.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: architecture constraints, noise tolerance, and gating criteria — prep for Wed 11/25 10am PT

Able to join Wed 10:00 PT. Quick notes:
- I'll pull p95 perf runs for the 7B quantized profile and include a short note about how batching during bursts affects tail latency.
- For KMS: Dedicated supports customer KMS via our key-rotation proxy (engineering caveat: we need a service account and one-time Vault setup), Private gets full HSM option. I'll draft a short slide that maps steps and estimated eng effort.
- On PHI boundary: bring the VPC peering checklist and what logs/audit endpoints we can expose for their compliance team.

See you Wed.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
